# launchR: full text for agents

launchR starts an R package with tests, CI and GitHub files in place, or adds ready-made CI and a quality gate to a package that already exists. It is free and open source under the MIT licence.

- Site: https://launch-r.web.app/
- Source: https://github.com/insightsurge/launchR
- Skill for agents: https://launch-r.web.app/SKILL.md
- Author: Harsh Verma, InsightSurge

## Who it is for

- People writing their first R package, with or without GitHub experience.
- Maintainers who want shared CI in place of their own workflow files.
- Developers building private packages inside a company.

## How it works

1. Answer five questions on the site: package name, a one-line title (plus an optional longer description), author, GitHub user or organisation, and plan.
2. Download a zip named after the package. It is built in the browser, with no account and no server, and nothing typed into the form leaves the browser.
3. Follow the next-steps page to put the package on GitHub. Only GitHub is supported.

The command line in the repository (`Rscript cli/launchr.R new mypkg`) makes the same package.

## Plans

| Plan | For | Quality gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public, going to CRAN | Open-source package authors | CRAN rules |
| Public, not for CRAN | Packages installed from GitHub | Internal rules |
| Private for now | Public and CRAN later | CRAN rules |
| Private for good | Company or personal packages | Internal rules |

## Checks

Each check is a short workflow file in the package that calls a shared workflow in launchR, pinned to an exact version. Dependabot proposes updates for new minor and major launchR versions; patch versions arrive with the next minor one.

| Check | What it does | On by default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `r-cmd-check` | R CMD check | Yes |
| `lint` | Style, docs in sync and spelling | Yes |
| `secret-scan` | Catches passwords and tokens committed by mistake | Yes |
| `coverage` | Measures how much code the tests run | Yes |
| `no-suggests` | Checks the package works without its optional packages | Yes |
| `full-tests` | Runs every test, including the browser, snapshot and extended tests CRAN skips, with Chrome for browser tests | Yes |
| `r-cmd-check-extended` | Weekly R CMD check on more systems, with the extended tests (Mac and Windows for public packages, Linux only for private ones) | Yes, except for private packages that won't go to CRAN |
| `pkgdown` | Builds and publishes a package website | When a website is chosen |

## Customise a plan

Each plan sets defaults. On the site, pick a plan and download, or choose Customise a plan and go through four more steps (Checks, Issues and checklists, README and website, Extras); on the command line, a flag changes them:

- The checks, their R versions and systems, the minimum R version, and the weekly time.
- The CI report comment: one comment on each pull request with the results of the chosen checks. On by default.
- The licence: MIT, or proprietary (all rights reserved). Proprietary is the default only for a private package that won't go to CRAN.
- README badges: R-CMD-check, Lifecycle, Codecov, CRAN version, CRAN downloads, R-universe and "Set up with launchR". R-CMD-check and Lifecycle are on by default for public packages, and the "Set up with launchR" credit for every package. On the site the credit is always on; the command line can leave it out with `--badges`.
- The website's navbar items.
- Which issue forms and labels (five forms and twelve labels by default, each chosen one by one), and which stage checklists the package gets (a plan starts with its own; Set up opens on the first run for every plan; Next release opens from the start for a package not for CRAN and once the package is on CRAN for one that is; QC adds its sections to Next release, is offered to every plan and is on by default for a private package that won't go to CRAN).

## Existing packages

launchR can supply the CI files only. `R/`, `tests/` and `DESCRIPTION` are left alone.

## Coming soon

- A snapshot option that copies CI into the repository for teams that must freeze it.
- Pasting a public GitHub link to see what a package is missing.
